parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to determine the effects of factors related to stream drying and permanence on colonization and extinction dynamics of a crayfish species, and I am using the unmarkedMultFrame function in unmarked to get at this question. I collected presence/absence data at 23 sites for 4 seasons (summer 1, fall 1, summer 2, fall 2) which are my primary periods, and I have 2 secondary sampling surveys for each season. 

I am having issues with the null model estimate for extinction probability. The estimate I get for null extinction is 0.0925. Since this is not an estimate that I typically see (e.g. ~ 0.100 - 0.999), I am wondering if there is something wrong, or if the null extinction estimate for this species is in fact 0.0925. The naive occupancy rates are very high (0.74 - 0.93), so I am also wondering if this is contributing to the issue. 

Here is code output for reference. I greatly appreciate any input and can give more context if needed. Thanks!

> # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Build an unmarkedmultFramOccu model ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ > Fmar_unmarkedMultFrame <- unmarkedMultFrame(y = as.matrix(Fmar_detection_history), +                                            numPrimary = 4, +                                            obsCovs = list(substrate = substrate, depth = depth, +                                                           wtpres = wtpres), +                                            siteCovs = site_covs[2:6], +                                            yearlySiteCovs = list(Wt_Pres = Wt_Pres, +                                                                  Cum_Precip_1wk = Cum_Precip_1wk, +                                                                  Precip_Freq_1mo = Precip_Freq_1mo, +                                                                  Season = Season, +                                                                  Site_Depth = Site_Depth)) Warning message: yearlySiteCovs contains characters. parts:
hi Leah,
 That estimate seems ok to me. Although I don't know much about crayfish , for a site to go extinct the entire local population would have to die off. Your result says there is a 9% chance that this happens between primary periods (seasons).  Seems like a sensible result.
 I'm curious if you have estimates from the literature that someone has published?
